minor.issue: The source text shows AJSM 2022 pages 1-8 with no volume or issue. The 50(9):2526-2533 details cannot be verified from the text.

It does not mention the adjustment for concussion history and height, that the study ran at two Division I sites, or that the career-duration calculation differed by site (age minus eAFE at one site).
It is thin, with no sample size, age or career-duration descriptives.

Presenting gait speed and stride length as 'reference values' goes slightly beyond the source. The authors only note that the values fell within the normal range for healthy collegiate athletes, citing prior work.
Volume and issue are left unstated. That is accurate to the extracted text but incomplete.

note: Both records are accurate on the null associations (b=-0.004, P=.35; b=-0.003, P=.57). B adds verified detail (n=168, age 19.2, career 10.6 years, covariates, eta-squared <=0.017, the 5-year exclusion), while A gives somewhat stronger caveats against using normal gait as a reassurance about brain health.
